doc.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016

chapter: Playing with Fame and Kim Parker
title: Playing with Georgie Fame and the song 'On a Misty Night'
summary: Touring with Georgie Fame, easy charts, and the Tadd Dameron tune that stuck in Rydin's head.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Oh here’s an odd one: Bent Fabric.
He was actually a Danish guy.
He had that piano hit “The Alley Cat.” But it might not have gotten into your consciousness. What about Georgie Fame?

So he is very easy to play with. He also brought easy scores to read. I remember the first time, we hadn’t played that much but we played a couple of times. We made a tour. The first time I played with him we were supposed to do a radio recording, and at the same time a whole night at a jazz club, three sets or something like that. So we rehearsed. We rehearsed in the afternoon, and there was also two horns. So we got some arrangements. And it was a lot of things. I mean a whole night of music, it was a lot of things really. And then there was one song, what’s the name — “On a Misty Night” and that was only the harmonies. C major, E minor, A flat major, D minor 7. Very easy to read. 32 bars. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

And we rehearsed that song. And then when I came home at night after playing, of all this music, it was this song that went in my head. [humms] It’s a very, very simple song in a way, but still unique, it’s Tadd Dameron. I wrote it down, and he sang it very straight in a slow/medium tempo and with nothing special, but it was nice and it was a lot appreciated by the audience. And the day after, I told him this story. Do you know which song I was thinking about, it was “On a Misty Night.” And he said, “Yeah, that happens all the time. It’s always popular by all musicians. It’s nice to improvise on. It’s simple but it has some challenges and some character, some definite character. So it’s a nice song, really.
I’ll have to check it out. I didn’t even know he did that kind of music. We’re mostly familiar with a couple of his hits.
Yeah but he did a lot of jazz, and a lot of vocalese. You know, like Jon Hendricks things.
Oh, Jon Hendricks, one of my favorites.
